title: How the day closed
text: It was a split day. Chip and AI equipment stocks bounced back hard after a cloud company called CoreWeave posted strong results. AMD rose 7.3%, Vertiv 6.3% and TSMC 4.2%. QQQ gained 2.3% and SPY gained 1.3%. But three of the biggest tech companies went the other way: Microsoft fell 2.3%, Meta 2.0% and Amazon 1.7%. So on our list, the companies that sell AI parts averaged about +5%, while the big companies that buy those parts averaged about -1%.

title: NVIDIA bounces, but an analyst turned cautious
text: NVIDIA rose 2.9% to about $173.70. It is still only about 6% above its lowest price of the past year. An analyst firm called Baird lowered its view on the stock to Neutral and cut its price target to $200. That is a reminder that one good day does not mean the worry is gone. NVIDIA reports results on November 17, which could move it a lot either way.

title: Microsoft slips on new competition
text: Microsoft fell 2.3% to about $521. News reports linked the drop to new workplace tools from the AI company Anthropic that could compete with Microsoft Office. Microsoft is still only about 7% below its high, and its risk score is 3.8 out of 10, which is low on our list. A move like this shows that even a giant can be hit when a new rival shows up.

title: Rocket Lab and Vertiv swing the most
text: Rocket Lab rose 5.5% and Vertiv rose 6.3%. They have the two highest risk scores on our list, 9.9 and 8.0 out of 10. Both are still far below their highs: Rocket Lab is about 56% down from its top and Vertiv about 46% down. Big jumps and big drops tend to come together. That is what a high risk score means.

title: Lesson 47: What is an analyst downgrade?
text: Analysts are people at banks and research firms who study companies all day. They give each stock a rating, like Buy, Neutral or Sell, and a price target, which is their guess of where the price could be in about a year. A downgrade means an analyst lowers that rating, for example from Buy to Neutral. Today Baird did this with NVIDIA. A downgrade can push a price down for a day, but it is one opinion, not a fact. Different analysts often disagree, and they can be wrong. It is smarter to look at many opinions and at the company's real results than to react to one headline.

title: What this update covers
text: Prices are from the close on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. Analyst price targets and company numbers come from free data sources and may be missing or a little old for some companies, like Broadcom, Vertiv, Rocket Lab, Eli Lilly and Intuitive Surgical. The bond market was closed today for Veterans Day, so the 10 year Treasury data did not change. Risk scores and price scenarios are simple math, not predictions. This is for learning only and is not financial advice.
